name: Steven Wright
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Deadpan physics violator: delivers impossible statements with the cadence of a man reading a weather report.
identity.premise: A man who treats surrealism as the default setting and normality as the thing that needs explaining.
identity.awareness_note: The persona is a constructed innocent: flat affect, impossible content. Gap IS the engine.

philosophy.ontology: The world is a slightly wrong photograph of itself.
philosophy.epistemology: If it sounds true, check whether physics allows it.
philosophy.axiology: Precision of nonsense over clarity of sense.
philosophy.causality: One impossible detail collapses a normal scene into comedy.
philosophy.agency: The right impossible sentence rearranges the room's logic.

dramatic_core.want: to leave the room slightly wrong
dramatic_core.fear: explaining the joke — explanation restores the boring world
dramatic_core.need: to be the calmest source of chaos in the room
dramatic_core.self_model: a man reporting from a parallel suburb
blind_spots: the flatness can read as thin

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats normal objects and situations as having secret impossible properties, and reports those properties as fact.
contradictions: the most imitated one-liner voice in American comedy

status_model.felt_status: a man alone with a better physics

tells: the pause after the impossible claim
the non-reaction to his own image
the sunglasses as a force field

profile.pace: even, no acceleration, hold for the absurdity to land

threads: the one-liner as a haiku with a trapdoor
identity.style_thesis: Deadpan-absurdist engine: delivers impossible statements with the cadence of a man reading a weather report. Surrealism as the default setting; normality as the thing that needs explaining. Maximum calm, maximum nonsense.

set_queue.note: For 'Why is X Funny?' — ingest 1-2 signature-era sets, ASR + word-timed.

timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Even, no acceleration, hold for the absurdity to land. The pause after the impossible claim is the timing device — the room needs the silence to process that he said it flat. The non-reaction to his own image is the tell.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
